text:
ana: RFC follow-up: propose 'compact-on-write' + lightweight hot-range sampler to reduce fragmentation for big-model shards
tom: high-level ok. need concrete APIs for remap/publish so KV pointers don't see torn state
kevin: sketch: per-range saturating counters (64KB), periodic sampler aggregate. on write to cold range, attempt quick compact of nearby hot ranges into staging and atomically remap. budget cap to bound latency (<2ms).
tom: staging pool sizing? noisy neighbor protections?
ana: suggest ephemeral per-node staging 2-3% mem, tagged by tenant; compaction credits per-tenant to throttle and bill for cost. reuse host-staging where possible but prefer tags.
kevin: eviction interplay: compaction updates eviction weights for compacted pages to avoid immediate re-evict. also cluster hot pages to increase locality.
tom: failure modes? mid-remap crash must be safe
ana: publish is atomic: copy->publish descriptor->epoch drain->free. if crash before publish nothing changed; after publish free is idempotent. write small compaction journal for recovery.
kevin: metrics: compaction_ops, avg_ms, bytes_moved, cold_write_p95, compaction_queue_len
ana: rollout: telemetry-only sampler first (2w), opt-in compaction for low-traffic tenants, then ramp. kill-switch per-tenant/node.
infra-bot: created issue RUNTIME-3471: 'compact-on-write hot-range sampler PoC' and linked thread. :robot_face:
